solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Anger's hidden by Jerry's adversary, see, without excitement

indicators.note: something hidden by another thing is enclosed within it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Tom is the cat forever chasing Jerry the mouse in the cartoons
anger is ire, and the 's gives IRE'S
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the crossword's favourite cathedral city

explanation.surface: A cartoon cat calmly conceals his fury at the mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom and Jerry are the cartoon cat and mouse; Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, so a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a tedious, wearying way means doing it with no thrill at all.

clue.text: Not cross for a moment

definitions.meaning: on a marked paper the alternative to a cross is the opposite check mark

explanation.definitionFit: A check mark signals correct rather than wrong, and in British speech the same word means a brief instant.

clue.text: Cluster of hair girl fixed with net

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rearranged or doctored, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman secures her curls with a hairnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges the letters of GIRL and NET together.
explanation.definitionFit: A curled lock of hair hanging down is a small bunch of strands.

clue.text: One of a couple in court to suppress noise?

definitions.text: One of a couple in court

parts.note: to squash a protest is to suppress it
a racket is a loud din

explanation.surface: Someone in a law court seeks to silence a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but it is the walled court where two players each hold a bat for the indoor ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the two players in an indoor squash match carries one, so it is one of a pair on court.

clue.text: Disorderly lot going round hill on American vehicle

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: An unruly crowd travels around a hill on a US vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, a word found mainly on Dartmoor and elsewhere in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor bus is an old name for a motorised bus, a passenger road vehicle.

clue.text: Row securing a good amount of editorial matter

indicators.note: securing means holding in, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: An argument wins a decent quantity of newspaper copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like an argument, but here it is a line; 'securing' puts A and G inside LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Linage is the number of printed lines of text, a measure of how much copy a page carries.

clue.text: Country protected by formal institution

indicators.note: something protected by words is held within them, so the letters lie hidden inside

explanation.surface: A nation is sheltered by an official establishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' points to the letters running across 'formal institution'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African republic.

clue.text: A solitary type, male engaged as hospital worker no more

indicators.note: engaged as in held within, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: a loner keeps to themselves

explanation.surface: A reclusive man takes a job at a hospital in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' looks like betrothal or hiring but puts M inside LONER, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital social workers in Britain were once called by this title, which has since fallen out of use.

clue.text: Tories rule in unsettled fashion, lacking clear purpose

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Conservatives govern without any firm direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in unsettled fashion' rearranges TORIES RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undecided and wavering has no firm aim in mind.

clue.text: Adviser continued to want leader of empire restricted

indicators.note: the first piece wants the second held in, so it encloses it

parts.note: a sultan rules an empire such as the Ottoman one

explanation.surface: A counsellor still hopes to see an emperor's power curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' puts SULTAN inside CONT, the abbreviation used at the foot of a page that runs on.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a specialist hired to give expert advice.

clue.text: Ruler of grim empire, backward-looking

indicators.note: backward-looking says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A despot presides over a bleak realm that looks to its past.
explanation.walkthrough: The run RIME spans 'grim empire'; 'backward-looking' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, a sovereign.

clue.text: One taking this one won't gain much ground

definitions.text: One taking this one won't gain much ground

parts.words: One taking this one won't gain much ground
parts.note: reads like a soldier failing to advance, but describes acquiring a small parcel of farmland

explanation.surface: A soldier making this capture won't advance far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'gain ground' suggest a battle, but the clue is about buying a small farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A smallholding is a little farm, so whoever takes one acquires only a modest plot of land.

clue.text: Drinks given special trade promotion, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is taken from the front and put at the end

parts.note: a sale is a period of cut prices offered by shops

explanation.surface: Beverages are put on a discount, the earliest arrivals served last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of SALE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Engineers, fellows this person's put in fighting units

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: gents are men
this person is the speaker, I, and 's gives I'M, I am

explanation.surface: Army engineers and other men are drafted into combat formations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter speaking of themselves, a common crossword convention; the Royal Engineers is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Regiments are permanent army units of soldiers.

clue.text: Celebrate outside club, jabbering

indicators.note: the first piece goes outside, around the second

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: Revellers sing round a nightclub, babbling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a nightclub, but it is the golf club for the green; 'outside' wraps SING round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputtering speech comes out in fast, confused bursts, which is what babbling is.

clue.text: Dwindle as favourite with little energy facing defeat

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
E is the abbreviation for energy, a 'little' version of the word
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: The favourite, low on stamina, faces a beating and fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' just sets ROUT beside PET and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to diminish gradually until nothing is left.

clue.text: Peer endlessly into Cornish river with pretty plants?

indicators.note: the first piece is put into the other

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A nobleman stares and stares into a Cornish stream lined with blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a verb, to stare, but it is a nobleman; the Fal flows into the sea at Falmouth in Cornwall, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something decorated with flowers, a dress or a display, is described as flowery; the question mark marks the loose definition.

clue.text: A right troublesome goddess gets cut off

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A mischievous goddess is excluded despite her entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is not R but LIEN, a legal claim; ATE is the Greek goddess of folly.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to estrange them, isolating them from others.

clue.text: Fish crossing river or ditch

indicators.note: the first piece crosses, spanning around, the second

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish swims across a river or a drainage channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside TENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow channel dug in the ground.

clue.text: The personification of love at home admitting love is dying away

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: in means at home
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: The god of love finds romance fading even at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts O (love, nil in tennis) inside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is a gradual wearing away, a slow fading of something.

clue.text: I will be in this set filling in crosswords

definitions.text: I will be in this set filling in crosswords

parts.words: I will be in this set filling in crosswords
parts.note: reads like a solver at work, but the letter I belongs to the set of letters used to fill the grid

explanation.surface: A solver promises to be busy with puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' seems to be a person, but it is the letter I, one of the twenty-six used to fill any grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters from A to Z form the set from which every crossword entry is written.

clue.text: Pub gets to profit from special deal

parts.note: a bar is a pub
to gain is to profit

explanation.surface: A pub stands to make money out of an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'from' are only joining words between the pub and the profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an advantageous purchase or agreement.

clue.text: Fair prohibition restricts extremist characters beginning to agitate

indicators.note: restricts means hems in, so the first piece holds the rest

parts.note: a bar is a ban
A and Z are the letters at the two extremes of the alphabet

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A ban on radicals at a fete starts to stir trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremist characters' are the letters at each end of the alphabet, not radicals; 'beginning to' takes only the opening letter of 'agitate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a market or charity sale, the sense of a fair.

clue.text: Lover no longer one to chide, that's clear

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to rate someone is to scold them, an old sense

explanation.surface: A former partner is the one to scold, and that clears things up.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE, meaning to berate, is an old word now mostly found in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to clear them of blame.

clue.text: Bird in vessel on lake

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the vessel follows the lake

parts.note: Noah's ark is the vessel

explanation.surface: A bird perches in a boat on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts ARK after L.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a songbird, famous for singing in flight.

clue.text: More than one runner misses out, lacking power

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to skip is to miss out
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Several athletes don't turn up, lacking energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete, but a ski runs on snow; 'lacking' takes P out of SKIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Skis are the long runners that glide over snow, and the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Woman from Dublin maybe that's ditched husband

indicators.note: something ditched is dropped, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: Dublin is in Ireland, so its people are Irish

explanation.surface: A Dublin woman has left her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's ditched' removes H from IRISH; 'maybe' marks Dublin as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the clue's woman is a female first name borrowed from the flower and the Greek rainbow goddess.

clue.text: Wild beast may be seen here in the distance, one going in a flash

definitions.text: Wild beast may be seen here

indicators.note: the pieces go into the other one

parts.note: a spark is a flash of light
afar means far away
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild animal is glimpsed far off, one darting by in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: The flash is split around the far-off one, leaving its last four letters as the second word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari park is a zoo where wild animals roam large enclosures and visitors drive through.

clue.text: Group from north sitting in silence

indicators.note: sitting in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

explanation.surface: A party from the north sits in quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting in' puts N inside GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a band of people, a group.

clue.text: Strange fee negotiated for uncommitted participants

indicators.note: terms that are negotiated are reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd fee is agreed for players not bound to any team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'negotiated' rearranges STRANGE FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Free agents are players or people not under contract to any club or party.
